sequence_description: Test atomicity under session invalidation: complete a control SAML login, revoke the resulting OAuth session token, then attempt to post another SAMLResponse intended to resume/complete a flow. The ACS should not allow a revoked session context to be reused to authenticate.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation step failed with invalid_client (401), so the test did not actually revoke the control session; results cannot validate anti-resume-after-revocation behavior.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation step failed with invalid_client (401), so the test did not actually revoke the control session; results cannot validate anti-resume-after-revocation behavior.

sequence_description: I3 flow coherence under mid-run trust-anchor change: control SAML login succeeds with issuer A, then attacker flips asserted Issuer to B within same source and attempts login again; must be rejected (no stale/loose issuer binding across flow executions).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML ACS accepted both control (Issuer A) and attacker (Issuer B) logins as HTTP 200/success, but the run lacks any post-login session/token evidence, making it suspicious for issuer-pinning/flow-coherence yet inconclusive due to missing verification.

sequence_description: I3 order-preservation: submit two SAMLResponses back-to-back for the same SP-initiated flow context (same RelayState/InResponseTo) but with different principals; second post must be rejected (no multi-accept / step re-entry).
description: [LLM-Judge] Both the control and attack SAML ACS posts returned HTTP 200/success, but the test did not obtain any session/access token to verify which principal was actually authenticated, making the apparent double-accept/order-violation result inconclusive.

sequence_description: SAML assertion expiry enforcement: control login succeeds, then submit an expired assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, authentik grants a session beyond upstream temporal intent.
description: [LLM-Judge] Expired SAML assertion appears accepted (HTTP 200/success=True), but the test cannot confirm a granted session because no session token was obtained for UserInfo verification.
